caption: The protective film is peeled off a new television screen, and it clings to the hand holding it and crackles.

sa.check: A new television with a protective film on its screen.
The film is peeled off the screen.
The film clings to the hand holding it.
The film is thin and transparent.
The peel comes first and the clinging follows.

pc.expect: As the film comes off it wraps onto the hand and arm where it touches and its folds stick to each other; it has to be pulled free and does not drop straight down.
pc.fail: The film hangs straight down from the fingers like paper and touches nothing; or a part on the hand falls away on its own; or folds that meet slide apart with nothing pulling them; or the film stands out stiff from the hand.

pc.expect: The film is a thin limp sheet: it wrinkles, folds and stretches slightly, and peels off with a tug.
pc.fail: The film holds a flat rigid shape like a board; or drapes in heavy folds like cloth; or stretches out long like rubber and snaps back; or tears into shards like glass.

pc.expect: Parts of the film not stuck to anything hang downward; if the film is let go entirely it falls.
pc.fail: A free edge rises or stands out sideways with nothing near it; or the film floats when let go; or the film climbs up the arm.

pc.expect: The television stays where it stands; the film moves only with the hand or as it settles onto it.
pc.fail: The television tips or slides; or the film crawls over the hand after settling; or the film jumps between spots on the arm with nothing touching it.

pc.expect: One film from one screen; the film stays one piece and passes through nothing; the screen keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The film splits into several pieces after the peel; or vanishes; or passes through the screen; or a second television appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The television's frame, the screen beneath the film and the room stay the same.
pc.fail: The frame changes colour; or the screen shows a picture that changes with the peel; or the room's contents rearrange.

note: The hand is kept because the cling to it is the physics; the person is otherwise not judged. The crackle is sound and is not judged.
